Extraction shooter, through the nature of one there is a lack of variety and a lack of progression, while marathon has better progression then arc raiders as it doesn't take nearly as long to grind it still is small improvements and upgrades that are still used in the same old gameplay, drop in grab, grab shit, get out. At the moment, MARATHON is neither a disappointment nor the next big thing – but it is a surprise. The fact that Bungie has committed itself to a design philosophy that is so merciless to the player in this prestigious project defies all reason. But the result feels coherent, plays extremely smoothly, and (for now) seems to have more up its sleeve than the first few hours suggest.

Is it better than other extraction shooters? No. But it has character, style, and good ideas. Are the absurdly high production costs noticeable? Only to a limited extent. Under the current circumstances, will it be able to compete with its genre counterparts and gain a player base large enough to survive? Will it be given the time to evolve? That remains to be seen. For my part, I'm along for the ride.

Update after approx 120 hours:

The 2nd season brought a lot of improvements. Especially progression now feels much better and less of a grind. It took me some time to understand how it's meant to be played. If you dig the tension and can handle the occasional bad couple of rounds, it can actually be quite rewarding. For my taste, it's a really, really good game.

I love this game as an extraction shooter, as an entry to the franchise, and as a game in general. The artstyle and worldbuilding is insane.

My ONLY gripe, and I mean ONLY, is the class/character system. Turning an extraction shooter into a hero game was not exactly something I had been hoping for, especially from an extraction shooter. I would've settled for abilities with customizable shells (as was originally promised), but instead I have to entirely avoid the Solos mode because half the players are invisible and the other half are using characters with insane mobility (Thief, lol). It gets frustrating when you're stuck on the same quest for a week because random fills refuse to go near your objective and solos you can't travel 50ft without encountering a player of some kind.

I really, REALLY like Marathon. But the class system has me burnt out. I'm tired of hero shooters, I'm tired of class based abilities. I'm tired of annoying jank that only adds to divide the playerbase more. I love all of the shells and characters Marathon has, but I hate them in gameplay, and this game would be better without a hero system. I cannot name an extraction shooter with some kind of class/character based mechanics and it's because it really just doesn't work that well.

It is a tragedy of modern gaming that Marathon, and Bungie have come be defined by their controversies, rather than their merits. I am not exaggerating when I say Marathon has some of the best game design accompanied with some of the most interesting lore and art style of 2026. I was surprised how much classic Marathon lore/DNA was actually in this and I can only suspect Jason Jones played a Signiant role in the writing.

It is absolutely not a perfect game as elements are certainly underbaked, like only have 3 maps and no area shooter/casual mode. Yet in spite of that this is easily one of the best multiplayer experiences on the market and I hope they find a way to weather the storm and develop a player base which will allow them to continue supporting the game.

I feel like this game has a lot of the really great structure of more hardcore extraction shooters like tarkov but with more systems to help players get back to the position they were after dying. The game needs a training map to test out the weapons and the UX needs some reorganization but this game clicked with me way more than I anticipated.

Phenomenal potential. Incredible art style, music, and sound design. I LOVE the world design and atmosphere. The gunplay is bungie-perfect, feeling just like old destiny for me. I love fighting the PvE enemies, but that's where the good ends.

They decided to make it an extraction shooter, even though the old IP was a campaign. I don't know if it was Sony's choice or what but it ruined the game. The gameplay loop just isn't fun, and PvP is excruciating with the way the map was designed, and shouldn't have been the focus. Not to mention the insane amount of grind needed to get to the boss, which is what drew me and my friends in in the first place.

I saw they're making a PvE only mode and I love that, so good job on trying to fix the huge issues with Marathon. But please work on a campaign, I wish you guys didn't cook so hard on the lore just to make it an extraction shooter that's heavily PvP focused.

Will look back once they release that December 2026 update.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period do not point to one clear reason, covering topics such as Linux BattlEye support, removed solo and casual modes, and hostile player encounters.

lines.F1: Marathon had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), Jun 2026
lines.F2: Jun 2026: 49% positive across 6,382 reviews (3,285 negative), against a usual 83% positive and 1,040 negative a month
lines.R1: (negative review, 1h played) "Bungie is ignoring a player base over a SINGLE TOGGLE SWITCH ON BATTLEYE. Battleye is fully supported on proton/linux but they refuse to enable it. If this is supposed to be Bungie's big comeback locking out an entire Linux desktop and Steam deck..."
lines.R6: (negative review, 5h played) "Nope. I'm done. I want to get in and do contracts and get out. After the initial Beginner point the game just pushes you into a bloodbath with people who's only interest is mowing down everyone around them. Not the type of game I want to be playing...."
lines.R13: (negative review, 20h played) "They added a solo pve mode that helped their player count rise a lot, it was a fun way to enjoy the game for many. But seems like Bungie hates fun so they decided to remove it and now even less people are playing it. They are just digging their own..."
lines.R14: (negative review, 350h played) "Bungie Devs are removing parts of the game that make it fun for some people. Their sponsored survival option has been removed after 3 weeks. The 'Casual' gamers are not going to have things to do and will end up leaving a very small playerbase...."

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (80%): players praise the gameplay and combat most.
The main complaint is the co-op, where many players object to forced PvP.

details.text: Recent reviews are a little less positive than all-time, yet complaints about gameplay and servers have eased.
New players are far less positive, at 40%, than players who have logged 10 hours or more.
